transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-08-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Orion - Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Orion - Infra Lead), Liam O'Neill (Orion - Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal / contract rollover conversation focused on adding APAC edge capacity, clarifying dedicated vs hosted options for low-latency storefront use cases, and confirming compliance docs for procurement. Agreed to pilot APAC edge with a limited reserved pool and run a 1M-token/day benchmark.

Topics: capacity upgrade, APAC edge region, contract rollover timelines, SOC2/KMS, pricing addendum, pilot benchmarks

Action items (short): Jenna to send pricing + APAC addendum; Marcus to share SOC2 & pen test summary; Carlos to share traffic profile; Liam to confirm procurement timing.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna: hey everyone thanks for joining on time. quick goal for today - sync on the contract rollover and the APAC edge ask, make sure we have a plan for the pilot and next steps.
[00:18] Priya: yeah thanks, um the main thing is we need predictable latency for our checkout flows in APAC and we have a new partnership that requires 99ms p95 or better, so we are thinking edge nodes or dedicated capacity there.
[00:32] Marcus: right, so just to be clear - we can do two approaches: hosted APAC region with burst capacity, or a dedicated APAC pool to guarantee throughput. dedicated gives you true isolation and predictable p95 but at a higher commit.
[00:45] Carlos: can you remind me of the minimum commit for a dedicated pool? I know our infra team has budgets but it's a bit tight right now.
[00:55] Jenna: yeah minimum is 4 GPUs reserved in our dedicated SKU, typical starting point. you can also do hybrid — reserved baseline plus burst on hosted — which usually helps the budget.
[01:10] Liam: are those GPUs in-region? our legal is gonna be picky about data residency and we want traffic for Asia to stay in-region if possible.
[01:20] Marcus: yes the APAC edge would be physically in the APAC region, and the control plane still sits in our US/owned control plane if you use Redwood Private we can flip to customer-managed control plane, but that is a separate private deployment discussion.
[01:36] Priya: hmm okay ok. on the contract rollover: we want to keep the same terms mostly but add the APAC addendum for the edge nodes and want to extend the term by 12 months. we also want better price protection for any model quantization or caching changes.
[01:54] Jenna: got it. we can draft an addendum for APAC capacity and a 12-month rollover. price protection for model changes we'll flag — usually tied to committed throughput not model internals, but we can propose guardrails.
[02:10] Carlos: quick technical question - for our workloads we use sequence lengths up to 2k tokens on cart recs and checkout. how does the runtime perform with that? will KV cache help?
[02:23] Marcus: yes KV cache helps a lot for repeated prefixes, but long sequences hit memory. our recommended path for 2k sequences is to use the optimized attention kernels we have and a dedicated pool, also quantization-friendly models. there was some chatter about "K V cash" in earlier notes - apologies the auto transcript mangled KV cache.
[02:40] Priya: ha yes the transcript already did that.
[02:44] Jenna: also to call out — if you want down to the 99ms p95 we recommend the dedicated APAC pool with autoscale headroom of 25% and prefix caching enabled. that combination has been used by similar retailers.
[03:02] Liam: pricing... can you ballpark the delta vs hosted?
[03:07] Jenna: ballpark dedicated will be around 1.6-2x the hosted per-token cost if fully committed, but you'll get the latency SLAs. Hybrid is maybe 1.1-1.3x depending on burst usage. we'll send a detailed pricing sheet.
[03:22] Priya: ok that helps. Procurement will also need SOC2 and pen test artifacts. do you have recent reports?
[03:29] Marcus: yes we have SOC 2 type II and a recent pen test summary. i'll bundle the cert and a redacted report. we also have KMS/HSM integrations — if you need customer-owned KMS we can support that in Private or via key wrap in Dedicated.
[03:45] Carlos: for HSM are there extra latency implications?
[03:48] Marcus: negligible for in-flight tokens; key ops are small surface. main impact is initial crypto ops on model load — usually trivial.
[03:56] Speaker 1: (mumble)
[03:58] Jenna: sorry who was that?
[04:00] Priya: that's me saying we also want SAML SSO for team access and RBAC controls.
[04:05] Marcus: yep we have SAML, SCIM, and RBAC support in console. we can enable a read-only role for analytics folks.
[04:14] Carlos: good. on the pilot: we propose 2 weeks of benching with 1M tokens/day to mimic peak traffic, and then gauge ops. how much telemetry do we get to instrument?
[04:26] Jenna: you'll get token-level cost and latency breakdowns, dashboards per-route, and trace hooks. plus we can give you exportable CSVs for your analytics.
[04:35] Priya: fine. I want to understand fallback behavior - if the APAC pool hits capacity what happens?
[04:41] Marcus: we have smart routing policies - you can set fallback to hosted region with slightly higher latency, or automatic scale triggers to spin more instances if commit allows. also can set priority queues.
[04:55] Liam: how long to get APAC provisioned if we sign the addendum?
[04:59] Jenna: once the PO is approved and the addendum signed, provisioning for a dedicated APAC pool is typically 7-10 business days; for hybrid we can enable a hosted APAC region in 48-72 hours.
[05:12] Carlos: ok that's helpful. one more infra ask — we do traffic encryption with our egress rules, any special networking config?
[05:20] Marcus: for Dedicated we provide a VPC peering option and private link; for Private you can run in your VPC. we'll share network diagrams in the packet.
[05:31] Priya: great. question from procurement: is there an early termination or rollover penalty? we may want a short grace window.
[05:39] Jenna: standard rollover has 30 days notice for scale-down, early termination fees vary by commitment level. we can put a clause in the addendum to allow a 60-day review window for APAC capacity in the first 3 months.
[05:52] Liam: that'd make legal happy.
[05:55] Priya: for the pilot bench — what metrics should we collect on our side?
[05:58] Marcus: latency p50/p95/p99, tail latency under load, token cost, error rate, and model output quality metrics tied to your prompts. we'll provide a bench script and sample prompts.
[06:12] Priya: cool. can you also include guidance on model quantization tradeoffs? we've seen some degredation with 8-bit in other infra.
[06:20] Marcus: yes we'll attach a quantization guide. for some models 8-bit int with calibrated inference is fine; for others you need per-workload evals. Redwood Optimize can suggest profiles based on your prompt set.
[06:34] Jenna: quick note — competitor question, Liam: you said you were also looking at BigCloudAI and Inferon?
[06:40] Liam: yes they came up in vendor evals. pricing is a bit lower at first glance but we prefer a predictable serving story.
[06:48] Jenna: understood — we can run a cost/lantency comparison in the addendum.
[06:52] Priya: ok next steps — timeline wise we want to sign the rollover in the next two weeks if possible. procurement timeline is tight but doable.
[07:02] Jenna: perfect. I'll send the updated pricing spreadsheet and APAC addendum by Monday, and Marcus will share the SOC2 and pen test summary. Carlos will send the traffic profile CSV and Liam will confirm PO window.
[07:13] Carlos: I'll get the CSV exported today.
[07:15] Liam: i'll speak to legal and try to get the approval calendar by Friday.
[07:19] Priya: schedule the pilot bench for the week of Sep 1st?
[07:23] Marcus: we can do Sep 1st, yes. that gives us time to provision and prep scripts.
[07:28] Jenna: great. any other blockers?
[07:31] Priya: none from me.
[07:33] Carlos: nope.
[07:35] Liam: no.
[07:36] Jenna: ok recap of explicit next steps — (1) Jenna send pricing + APAC addendum and draft clause for 60-day review window, (2) Marcus share SOC2 + pen test + quant guide + bench scripts, (3) Carlos share traffic QPS and seq-length distribution, (4) Liam confirm procurement calendar and PO window.
[07:57] Jenna: i'll also include links in the email: Pricing spreadsheet link: https://redwood.app/pricing/ORION, Security packet: https://redwood.app/security/packets/ORION (redacted), APAC addendum draft will be attached.
[08:15] Priya: thanks everyone, we'll look out for the email.
[08:18] Jenna: thanks, we'll follow up. bye.

End of transcript.
